transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Anytime I have to get on the freeway, I go out of my way to avoid it or white-knuckle my way through the drive, and it’s gotten to the point where it’s really disrupting my routine. It has just become too hard to manage on my own, so I realized I needed to talk to someone.
When you’re on the freeway, do you feel a sudden intense fear or panic specifically because of the freeway situation, or do you worry in many different areas of life most days?

It is definitely specific to the freeway, especially when I'm near big trucks or even just see an on-ramp sign. I don't really worry about other areas of my life; this intense panic and dread only happen in relation to the freeway since that crash.
When you’re facing the freeway, do you get physical panic symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, sweating, trembling, or feeling like you might lose control?

Yes, absolutely. Just seeing a freeway on-ramp or GPS directions makes my heart pound, my hands get clammy, and I feel this wave of dread. When I actually force myself to drive on it, I shake so much that I sometimes have to pull off at the next exit.
Since the crash, do you also have nightmares, flashbacks, or unwanted memories of the accident, or is the fear mainly limited to driving on the freeway?

The fear is really just limited to the freeway and things related to it, so I don't have nightmares or random flashbacks during my normal day. However, if I see a freeway on-ramp, look at highway directions on my phone, or get near a big truck, I get this sudden wave of dread that feels like I'm right back in that pileup.

Does this fear happen only with freeways and freeway-related cues, or does it also happen in other places where you feel trapped or unable to get help, like bridges, tunnels, elevators, or crowded enclosed spaces?

No, it’s really just limited to the freeway, on-ramp signs, and being near big trucks. I don't have any issues with elevators, crowded spaces, or other places where I might feel trapped. It is specifically the high-speed freeway driving and the fear of another crash that triggers my anxiety.

Do you also avoid or feel intense fear in other situations where you might be trapped or unable to escape, like bridges, tunnels, elevators, or crowded places, or is it only the freeway and freeway-related cues?

Like I mentioned, it is strictly the freeway and freeway-related cues that terrify me. I have absolutely no fear or avoidance when it comes to elevators, tunnels, or crowded spaces. It's just the high-speed freeway environment that triggers this reaction.

Do you fear only the freeway and things directly related to driving on it, or do you also feel intense fear in many other situations where you might be trapped or unable to escape, like bridges, tunnels, elevators, or crowded places?

It is truly just the freeway and being near big trucks that scare me. I don't feel this way on bridges, in tunnels, elevators, or crowded places at all. The fear is completely focused on highway driving and the risk of another crash.
Do you fear the freeway itself because it reminds you of the crash, or is the main fear being unable to escape or get help if something goes wrong while driving?

It's definitely about the freeway itself and the fear of getting into another horrific crash. When I'm on it, my brain is convinced I'm going to die or get hit by a truck, rather than worrying about being unable to escape or get help.

Do you also avoid or fear other situations where you are away from home or might need to travel alone, like buses, trains, open roads, or being far from familiar places, or is it only the freeway and freeway-related cues?

No, I don't fear buses, trains, or being far from home at all. My fear and avoidance are strictly limited to the freeway, GPS routes that include it, and being near big trucks. As long as I don't have to drive on the freeway to get there, I am perfectly fine traveling anywhere.

When you avoid the freeway, is it mainly because you fear a specific object or situation on the road itself, like driving at high speed or being near trucks, rather than fear of being embarrassed, trapped, or unable to escape?

Yes, it is entirely about the freeway itself and being near those big trucks. Ever since the crash I saw, my mind immediately jumps to the terrifying fear of dying in a horrific accident on the road. I don't worry at all about being embarrassed or trapped; it's just the fear of another crash.

Since the crash, do you have unwanted memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or feel like you are reliving the accident when you are not on the freeway, or is the fear only triggered by freeway-related cues?

No, I don't experience any nightmares, flashbacks, or feel like I'm reliving the accident when I'm away from those triggers. The panic and dread are strictly set off by freeway-related cues, like seeing an on-ramp sign, looking at GPS directions, or driving near big trucks.

Since the crash, have you had any other trauma symptoms like avoiding reminders because they bring back the event, feeling constantly on edge, being easily startled, or having negative changes in mood or sleep? Or is the anxiety only when you encounter freeway-related cues?

No, I don't feel constantly on edge, and my sleep and mood are completely fine in my day-to-day life. The intense anxiety, pounding heart, and shaking are strictly triggered when I encounter freeway-related cues, like seeing an on-ramp sign, looking at GPS directions, or being near big trucks. Outside of those specific driving situations, I don't experience any of those other symptoms.

The fear is situation-specific rather than generalized, and there is no evidence of broader trauma re-experiencing, hyperarousal, or avoidance of multiple trauma reminders to support PTSD, nor fear of multiple escape-limited situations to support agoraphobia. This is most consistent with specific phobia, situational type.
